michielssen1993.source: E. Michielssen, J.-M. Sajer, S. Ranjithan, R. Mittra, 'Design of lightweight, broad-band microwave absorbers using genetic algorithms', IEEE Trans. Microwave Theory Tech. 41(6/7), 1024-1032 (1993), doi:10.1109/22.238519. Database values transcribed from the reprints in [asi_dib_2010] Table 1 and [kankilic_karpat_2023] Table 1 (identical; also consistent with [amaya_correa_2013] Table 1, which prints only the 1 GHz values of materials 3-8 and lists materials 9-16 as mu_m*f_m^2*1e-3 and mu_m*f_m*1e-2 under mislabelled headings); the original's Table I has not been seen. Its Tables II-III and Fig. 7 were read from photographs (see original_tables).
michielssen1993.note_material_8: eps''(1 GHz) of material 8 is 6 in both reprints; Zong et al. 2024 (ACES J. 39(8), Table 1) prints 16, which is taken to be a typo.
michielssen1993.relaxation_model: eps = 15; mu' = mu_m f_m^2/(f_m^2 + f^2), mu'' = mu_m f f_m/(f_m^2 + f^2) (f, f_m in GHz) = mu_m/(1 + j f/f_m): a Debye term with mu_inf = 0

problem.objective: minimise the maximum of 20 log10|Gamma| over the band

references.asi_dib_2010: M. J. Asi, N. I. Dib, 'Design of multilayer microwave broadband absorbers using central force optimization', Prog. Electromagn. Res. B 26, 101-113 (2010), doi:10.2528/PIERB10090103
references.kankilic_karpat_2023: S. Kankilic, E. Karpat, 'Optimization of multilayer absorbers using the bald eagle optimization algorithm', Appl. Sci. 13, 10301 (2023), doi:10.3390/app131810301
references.zong_2024: Y. M. Zong et al., 'Optimization of multilayer microwave absorbers using multi-strategy improved gold rush optimizer', ACES J. 39(8), 708-717 (2024), doi:10.13052/2024.ACES.J.390806
references.amaya_correa_2013: I. Amaya, R. Correa, 'Optimal design of multilayer EMAs for frequencies between 0.85 GHz and 5.4 GHz', Revista de Ingeniería (Universidad de los Andes, Bogotá) 38, 33-37 (2013), ISSN 0121-4993; the traditional-PSO design is from Salazar & Mora (2011) as cited there
references.chamaani_2008: S. Chamaani, S. A. Mirtaheri, M. A. Shooredeli, 'Design of very thin wide band absorbers using modified local best particle swarm optimization', AEU Int. J. Electron. Commun. 62, 549-556 (2008), as reprinted in [asi_dib_2010] Table 10
references.goudos_2009: S. K. Goudos, 'Design of microwave broadband absorbers using a self-adaptive differential evolution algorithm', Int. J. RF Microwave CAE 19(3), 364-372 (2009), doi:10.1002/mmce.20357. Table I reprints the 16-material database and agrees with the values here (material 8: eps''(1 GHz) = 6). Uses Brest et al.'s self-adapting DE (jDE), max layer thickness 2 mm, 100 x 1000 generations, 20 trials; the frequency grid is not stated (0.1 GHz used here). Design DES1 (3-6 GHz, 0-10 deg, TE+TM, 6 mm; printed -25.98 dB) does not reproduce as printed (-13.2 dB here); with layer 3 = material 6 and layer 4 = material 15 it gives -26.1 dB, which suggests two misprints but is unverified. DES2 (0.5-8 GHz, 5 mm; materials 14/6/5/4/4, 0.431/1.438/1.143/0.507/1.479 mm; printed -20.26 dB) reproduces (-20.24 dB).
references.michielssen_1993: the original paper (see source above); table numbers follow the printed table numbers, whose captions are interchanged (see original_tables)

original_tables.seen: Tables II and III and Fig. 7 of the original, photographed from a screen by the user (2026-11-08) and read by eye; the photographs are not redistributed. Table I (the material database) and the text were not seen.
original_tables.caption_swap: The captions of Tables II and III are interchanged in print: the table captioned LF1-LF4 (0.2-2 GHz) holds HF1-HF4 and a row 'maximum reflection (2-8 GHz)', and the one captioned HF1-HF4 (2-8 GHz) holds LF1-LF4 and a row 'maximum reflection (0.2-2 GHz)'.
original_tables.layer_order: In the original, layer 1 is next to the PEC and layer 5 faces the incident wave. The 'layers' lists in this file are incident side first, so they read the printed columns from layer 5 to layer 1.
original_tables.thickness_grid: Every printed HF thickness is a multiple of 0.003 mm and every printed LF thickness a multiple of 0.006 mm, which suggests the GA's thickness quantisation.
original_tables.printed_maximum_reflection: The printed values are coarse (-23.5, -19.8, -17, -13 for HF1-HF4; -33, -21, -18, -14 for LF1-LF4). Against this engine the differences have both signs and reach 1.5 dB, so they are not calculation targets.

fig7_hf1_read_by_eye.points: maximum in band near 6.3 GHz at about -24.0 dB (computed 6.33 GHz, -24.02 dB); minimum near 7.75 GHz at about -27.1 dB (computed 7.75 GHz, -27.19 dB); about -5.7 dB at 0.1 GHz (computed -5.77 dB)
fig7_hf1_read_by_eye.conclusion: The paper's own HF1 curve agrees with this engine and disagrees with the -23.5 dB in its own Table II; why that number was printed is unknown.

original_tables.hf1_at_40_deg: Table II also prints '-16 at 40 deg' for HF1 without naming a polarisation; computed maximum over 2-8 GHz is -16.54 dB (TM) and -14.90 dB (TE).
original_tables.material_6_exponent: One reprint (Ingenieria y Universidad 18(1)) gives b = 0.596 for material 6 instead of 0.569. It does not explain HF1 (-23.84 dB) and it breaks the designs that reproduce (the Asi & Dib CFO and SADE designs move by more than 0.5 dB); 0.569 is kept.

A.how: coating-cli optimize, 16 candidates per layer, thickness 0.01-5 mm, total <= 5 mm; 4 rounds of --restarts 3, the last restarting from the previous best after the x0 fix (2026-11-07)

B.how: coating-cli optimize, 16 candidates per layer, thickness 0.01-2 mm (assumed limit), one run of --restarts 3; all three restarts reach the same 16/3/4 design

C.how: coating-cli optimize, 16 candidates per layer, thickness 0.01-10 mm, total <= 10 mm; 6 runs (first runs stalled at 5.8 mm; the best came from restarting the -18.29 dB design after the x0 fix)
